title: Prompt Thinking
tagline: Talking to AI is a skill — here's how to get good at it
summary: Most people get bad results from AI because they treat it like a search engine: one-word queries with no context. Prompt Thinking is a framework for communicating with AI the same way you'd brief a brilliant colleague — with context, constraints, format guidance, and examples.

pillars.name: Context
pillars.description: Tell the AI who it's talking to, what situation you're in, and why this matters. The more relevant context you provide, the more relevant the response will be.

pillars.name: Constraint
pillars.description: Tell the AI what NOT to do, what format you don't want, what audience to avoid. Constraints eliminate the most common failure modes.

pillars.name: Format
pillars.description: Tell the AI exactly how you want the output structured — bullet points, a table, a numbered list, a 3-paragraph essay. Don't make it guess.

pillars.name: Example
pillars.description: Show the AI one or two examples of what a good response looks like. This is the single most powerful technique in prompt engineering and is consistently underused.

keyQuestions: What does this AI need to know about my situation to give a great answer?
What are the ways this response could go wrong, and how do I guard against them?
What format would actually be useful for me — not just impressive?
Can I show the AI an example of what I actually want?
exampleInPractice: In workshops, I run a live exercise: everyone writes their current AI prompt, then we apply the Context → Constraint → Format → Example framework together. The quality improvement is immediate and visible. Participants who came in skeptical usually have their Aha! moment here. [NEEDS REVIEW BY MARLON]
